Coverage requires the correlation, in one tenant, of the table, the version-row UUID, the business approval id, the final approving request id, the SUCCESS `APPROVED → PUBLISHED` event and its actor, a distinct fresh confirmation returning the same PUBLISHED version, and a bounded subject state unchanged between before and after the confirmation; zero audit rows alone is not the proof. The class is enumerated as the `confirm` class of `backend/tests/support/audit_catalogue.py` with its publication literal (f-string-built by `lifecycle.transition`, verified by the walk at runtime, not by `action_literals()`). ### Decisions taken in B3 (D-77)

None of these opens a question. Each is the most reasonable default within the finisher's remit.

| Id | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| BSF-D-01 | **Merged file authoritative.** `docs/BUILD_SPEC.md` is generated by `research-harness/buildspec/merge_buildspec.py` and is the build contract the loop reads; `docs/build-spec/00-header.md`, the four author files and `90-appendices.md` are its maintained sources. Where the merged file and a source differ, the merged file governs. `--check` proves equality with a fresh merge. A supervisor item appended directly to the merged file (D-70) is copied into its source section before the next merge | One file for the loop; one diffable source per author (PHASES §0 "Assembly") |
| BSF-D-02 | **Merged layout.** Sections 1 to 7 of this header; the generated §8 phase index; the 27 phase sections in PHASES §3 order, each preceded by an HTML comment naming its source file; Appendix A, the generated table of contents of every item id and title in document order; Appendix B, the author metadata above the first phase heading of each author file (revision logs and the decisions BS1-D, B3-BS2, BS3-D and BS4-D that items cite), verbatim with headings demoted two levels; Appendix C, coverage waivers | The loop reads this header every iteration, so the long table of contents sits at the end; items cite author decisions, which must be greppable in the merged file |
| BSF-D-03 | **Parity selection before GPB.** GATE-CLO, GATE-RPS, GATE-SNP, GATE-LMG, their phase preambles, PHASES §1 row GPA and PHASES §4 row GATE-GPA run `make parity K="initial_allocation or pob_position or contract_position or cumulative_catchup or probe-P3-over-delivery-validation"` with 94 cases. PHASES §9 lists `legacy_probe` twice: probe P3 in GPA, probes P1, P2 and P4 in GPB | Review finding BSC-01; B3-BS2-04 invites the amendment. The 97-case selection could not be green before GPB-1, and fixing it earlier would pull GPB work forward (XR-19) |
| BSF-D-04 | **Captures `sf-21` and `sf-23`.** WEB-17 captures `sf-21` as `grace` on `/approvals` with the popover open over one unread `APPROVAL_ASSIGNED` item, inside the REQ-PLT-021 step. RFD-19 captures `sf-23` as `tomas` on `/settings/workspace` with the entity segment listbox of the context pill open | Review finding BSC-02. `grace` replaces the review's default `maya`, who holds no notification in the WEB seed (BS1-D-17), so her capture would show only the empty panel |
| BSF-D-05 | **Splits renumber the phase.** A split item keeps its id for its first part; the second part takes the next number, and every later item of the phase moves up by one. One script pass rewrote every reference in the four author files: prerequisites, GATE ranges and membership lists, decisions, notes, and the lowercase item ids in migration file names. Rev 1.0 revision-log rows keep their historical text. The rename map is in `docs/reviews/B3-buildspec-final.md` §3 | No `PROGRESS.md` exists yet, so ids are not evidence; BS-D-01 keeps unpadded sequential ids and reserves letter suffixes for supervisor items appended during the build |

## 1. Purpose and how items are ticked

This document orders the work of the Ralph loop that builds eRev Cloud 1.0 (`docs/00-GOAL.md`). The phase sections follow this header and the generated phase index (§8) in the order of PHASES §3. Every phase ends with a checkpoint item `GATE-<code>` (§6); the release phase REL ends the items (§7). Three appendices follow the items: A, the table of contents of every item id and title; B, the author notes and the author decisions that items cite; C, the coverage waivers.

The loop reads this header, the current item and the next item each iteration (PROMPT.md). It reads every other document only where an item cites it, by grep and offset reads.

An item is **done** only when all of the following hold:

1. Its acceptance criteria are met and every named test passes.
2. The dev-guide §10.4 checklist DG-DONE-01 to DG-DONE-12 is satisfied.
3. Every gate that §3 requires for the item's kinds is green, in a run made after the item's last change.
4. `PROGRESS.md` ticks it in the dev-guide §10.5 format, extended by BS-D-23:

   ```markdown
   - [x] <ITEM-ID> <item title>
     - Evidence: make ci OK (backend 612 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped; vitest 214 passed; build OK); make test-pg OK (388 passed)
     - Tests: backend/tests/domain/contracts/test_activation.py::test_ctl_004_activation_gate_blocks_missing_document (CTL-004)
     - REQs completed: REQ-CON-005
     - Commit: <short sha>
     - Spec questions: SPEC-Q-7 (04 T-CON-06 vs PRD SM-04; followed 04)
   ```

   Counts come from `.run/reports/<target>/report.json` (DG-GATE-04), never from memory.
5. It is committed with `PROGRESS.md` per DG-GIT-01 to DG-GIT-03.

Order: the loop finishes an item under **In flight** first; otherwise it takes the first unticked item in document order. It may complete several small items in one iteration, ticking and committing each separately, and never ends an iteration with `make ci` red (PROMPT.md).

A release-1.0 requirement counts for G1 when its completing item is ticked and every acceptance hint it carries has closed as PHASES §15 states.

## 2. Source precedence

| Question | Authority, highest first |
|---|---|
| Scope, definition of done, standing constraints | `docs/00-GOAL.md` |
| Conventions, policy defaults, rulings | `docs/01-DECISIONS.md`; the §7 and §8 amendments govern the text they amend |
| Priority and release of a capability | `docs/03-REQUIREMENTS.md` |
| Accounting behaviour and calculation | `docs/accounting/ENGINE_SPEC.md` with `ENGINE_SPEC_B.md` (one rank, D-74) and `docs/accounting/POLICIES.md`. **For numbers, the answer keys in `docs/accounting/answer-keys/` win over prose; a conflict is a spec question** |
| Enumeration literals, permission codes, problem slugs, finding and exception codes | `docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md` §3, T-PLT-11, §15.2 and §15.4 (D-73). Registry keys and option literals: POLICIES §1 (D-13a) |
| Code structure, kernel contracts, testing, gates | `docs/dev-guide.md` |
| Entities, tables, API surface | `docs/04-DATA_MODEL.md` → `docs/05-ARCHITECTURE.md` |
| Product behaviour, journeys, copy | `docs/02-PRD.md`. Route paths of SF ids: SCREENS (D-73) |
| Visuals and screens | `docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` → `docs/design/SCREENS.md` with `SCREENS_B.md` (one rank, D-74) |
| Legacy parity expectations | `docs/legacy/golden/golden-tests.json` with `docs/legacy/golden/deviations.json` and `docs/legacy/DEVIATIONS.md` (D-17, D-17a; G3; DG-PAR-01) |
| Order of work, acceptance tests, phase membership, gate scope | This BUILD_SPEC and `docs/build-spec/PHASES.md`. They never change behaviour that a document above fixes |
| Background only | `docs/research/*`, `docs/legacy/01` to `07`, `research-harness/`, `legacy-harness/` |

Rules:

1. **Reviews.** The reports in `docs/reviews/` record why the documents changed. The amended document governs; an objection file never governs (`docs/01-DECISIONS.md` §0).
2. **Conflicts.** The loop follows the higher-precedence document, records `SPEC-Q-<n>` with both references and the choice made (DG-DONE-12), and continues. It never edits a supervisor document (DG-GIT-05) or an expected value in the answer keys, `docs/legacy/golden/` or `deviations.json`. When it believes an expected value is wrong, it records the spec question and leaves the item unticked.
3. **Freeze (D-77).** The design documents and the answer-key corpus are frozen. Open-question ids are cited as `<document>:<id>` (D-76).

## 3. Gates

### 3.1 Gate table by item kind

An item has every kind that applies to it and runs the union of their targets. Targets and pass criteria are those of dev-guide §4.4 and §10.1.

| Id | Item kind | Targets | Pass criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| GK-01 | Every item | `make ci` | Five stages pass (DG-MK-ci; G2) |
| GK-02 | Schema: tables, columns, enum types or values, triggers, grants, RLS, partitions; subledger, ledger seals, audit or security-event chains; immutability | `make test-pg` | Every `pg` test passes, including DG-MIG-05 and DG-TST-20 to DG-TST-25 (G6; DG-DONE-02) |
| GK-03 | Backend command or route | `make openapi` in the same commit when routes or schemas change; `make test-pg` when the command depends on a DB invariant (DB-02 to DB-18) | `scripts/openapi_check.sh` clean inside `make lint`; pg tests pass (DG-DONE-03) |
| GK-04 | Engine helper or stage | `make ci` (engine tests sort first); `make properties K=<expression>` for each property the item adds or changes; `make answer-keys ID=<ids>` for each key the item names as passing | Selected properties and keys pass (D-71; BS-D-02) |
| GK-05 | Answer-key closure (AKS, EDS, PRP items) | `make answer-keys ID=<ids>` as the item names; unfiltered where PHASES §4 requires it | Every selected key passes; an unfiltered run reports zero corpus gaps (DG-AK-33) |
| GK-06 | Golden parity (GPA, GPB items) | `make parity K=<expression>`; unfiltered where PHASES §4 requires it | Every selected case passes and none is skipped (DG-PAR-09; G3) |
| GK-07 | Screen or design-system component | `make e2e SPEC=frontend/e2e/projects/screens.spec.ts`; for components also `make e2e SPEC=frontend/e2e/projects/design.spec.ts` | Specs pass; no serious or critical axe violation; the loop reads the light and dark screenshot of every capture the item added or changed, compares them with SCREENS, SCREENS_B and DESIGN_SYSTEM, and fixes deviations before ticking (DG-DONE-04; G8) |
| GK-08 | Journey | `make e2e SPEC=J-nn` (serial prefix semantics, DG-E2E-04) | Every step, acceptance item and alternate the item adds passes; screenshots read as in GK-07 |
| GK-09 | Performance | `make perf-seed` when the generator manifest changed, then `make perf` | Close ≤ 600 s; every DG-PERF-03 endpoint p95 ≤ 300 ms (G9) |
| GK-10 | Controls evidence and release stamping (SOP items) | `make controls-report`; `make release-manifest` | 49 of 49 controls have a passing tagged test (G7); the manifest is written (REQ-CTL-003) |
| GK-11 | Phase checkpoint `GATE-<code>` | `make ci`, `make test-pg` and the row of PHASES §4 for the phase | As that row states, on a clean tree (§6) |
| GK-12 | Release (REL items) | §7 | §7 |

### 3.2 Supervisor-only targets

`make audit-deps`, `make zap-baseline`, `make docker-build`, `make compose-verify`, `make tf-validate` and `make backup` are supervisor targets (D-48a; dev-guide §4.5; DG-MK-00h). The loop writes their scripts in DEP and never runs them (DG-FORBID-12). When an item needs one, the loop validates the artifacts offline and records `SUPERVISOR VERIFICATION NEEDED: make <target>` under **Supervisor verification needed**.

### 3.3 Gate discipline

- A red gate named by the item blocks the tick (DG-GATE-01). A regression outside the item is fixed before the next item starts (DG-GATE-02). A flaky test is a defect (DG-GATE-03).
- Targets bind only ports 8190, 5270, 8199 and 5279, and stop their processes by PID file (DG-RUN-10 to DG-RUN-15).

## 4. Cross-cutting rules for every item

- **XR-01 Migrations.**
  - One handwritten Alembic revision per item that changes the schema, created with `make revision MSG=<summary> ITEM=<item id>`. Its docstring names the item and the 04 ids created (DG-MIG-02, DG-MIG-03). Autogenerate is never used.
  - The revision is self-contained: tables with keys and indexes, composite foreign keys (NC-06), the RLS template (04 §1.4), the IM class and grants through `apply_class` (04 §1.5, §14.2), transition triggers (DB-03), monthly partitions (DG-MIG-10), and enum types created with their rev 1.2 values (04 §18 rules 5 and 6; DG-MIG-06). Objects appear in 04 §18 dependency order; a foreign key to a later table is added by the later table's revision.
  - `downgrade()` removes exactly what `upgrade()` created (DG-MIG-04). `test_single_head`, `test_upgrade_downgrade_upgrade` and `test_lint_after_upgrade` pass (DG-MIG-05).
  - Every new tenant table has a `ROW_BUILDERS` entry and joins the isolation suite (DG-TST-16, DG-TST-20). Every DB invariant it enforces has `test_db_<nn>_<slug>` pass and violation tests (DG-TST-23).
  - An index of a tenant table has a key the row-level-security policy can use (04 NC-20; DG-KRN-DB-10; rev 1.112): the columns compared with leakproof operators stand in front, an enumeration or a `numeric` column last, a status or a kind a read asks for is the predicate of a partial index. `test_nc_20_every_index_of_a_table_with_a_policy_can_be_used_under_it` passes, and a read that depends on the index has a plan test read as `erev_app`.
  - Migrations seed only global catalogues (DG-MIG-07). A table named in the 04 §14.3 provisioning seed extends `tenant.provision` in the same item (BS-D-12).
- **XR-02 Command pattern.**
  - Every state-changing operation, from any channel, is a handler that runs DG-CMD-01 to DG-CMD-08 in order: authorize, load and lock, validate (collect every finding), compute (at most one engine call per group), persist append-only, audit (one event per affected object), emit (rows only), commit through `run_command`.
  - Command routes use `command(...)`. They require `Idempotency-Key`; a missing key returns 422 `validation-failed` with `rule_id` `API-C-04` (DG-KRN-IDEM-01). Mutable resources require `If-Match` (API-C-08).
  - Decision and fact-capture commands follow DG-CMD-09 and DG-CMD-10. Routes hold no domain logic (DG-CMD-11). Queries never write and apply `as_of` and `known_at` (DG-CMD-13; API-C-10).
- **XR-03 Money.**
  - `Decimal` end to end; money is a string on the wire with an explicit currency, and a JSON number for money returns 422 (REQ-PLT-031). Stored types are `erev.money`, `erev.exact` and `erev.fx_rate` (D-11).
  - The engine holds exact values as `Fraction` and posted values as integer minor units, with `FloatOperation` trapped (DG-ENG-03). Rounding happens only through `erev_engine.money` (ALG-01; DG-ARC-06). Minor units come only from `ISO_4217`.
  - The frontend never converts a money string to a number, and totals come from the API (DG-FE-08).
- **XR-04 Registry.**
  - Policy and platform values are read only through `erev_api.registry.resolve` (dev-guide §5.15) and, in the engine, through `ctx.policies.value` (ENGINE_SPEC CV-17). Keys and option literals are exactly those of POLICIES §1 and T-PLT-31 (D-13a).
  - `backend/erev_api/registry/policies.py` is generated by `make registry-seed` and never edited by hand (DG-LAY-07). No other code holds a policy default literal.
  - Behaviour switches are policy values, never tenant ids, environment variables or legacy flags (DG-ENG-09). Configuration changes follow the SM-04 lifecycle under approval (REQ-POL-003).
- **XR-05 Explainability.** Every engine output value has a trace node with a formula id, and `reevaluate` reproduces it (DG-ENG-04; PROP:P14). Parity measure names equal column names (DG-PAR-05). Every persisted computed measure is served by `/explain` (API-R-49), and every computed figure on screen sits in `<ExplainTrigger figureRef>` (DG-FE-15; REQ-UX-005). A figure without a trace path is a defect.
- **XR-06 Identifiers verbatim.** Enumeration literals, permission codes, problem slugs, and finding and exception codes are written exactly as 04 §3, T-PLT-11, §15.2 and §15.4; route paths and screen ids exactly as SCREENS §0.4; copy exactly as SCREENS, SCREENS_B and PRD §5.5; `data-testid` values per SCREENS SCR-TID-02 to SCR-TID-04 (D-73; DG-READ-03). Where another document spells a literal differently, the owner's spelling is used and a spec question is recorded. The drift tests DG-ARC-09 and DG-ARC-13 stay green.
- **XR-07 Tests and markers.**
  - Test layout follows DG-TST-01 to DG-TST-05; engine tests request no database fixture (DG-TST-18).
  - `parity`, `answer_key`, `property`, `pg` and `perf` are applied only through module `pytestmark` in their directories (DG-TST-07). `@pytest.mark.control("CTL-nnn")` marks a test of the control: the tests tagged for a control exercise its failure path — at least one of them — and a tagged test may assert a clause of the control's row operating (DG-TST-06, dev-guide rev 1.252).
  - `skip`, `xfail` and `skipif` are forbidden in parity, answer-key, property, pg and control tests (DG-TST-09). Tests over 10 s carry `slow` (DG-TST-08). A failing Hypothesis example is pinned with `@example` before the fix (DG-PROP-02).
  - API tests use `committed_db` and fresh tenants; factories create data through commands (DG-TST-13, DG-TST-16). No network (DG-TST-15); frozen clock (DG-TST-14).
  - Named tests are binding for evidence (BS-D-22). CHK rows have `test_chk_<nnn>_<slug>` (DG-ENG-11), and `TC-` hints have `test_tc_<doc>_<nn>_<slug>` (BS-D-21).
  - Never weaken, skip or delete a test, and never edit an expected value, to make a gate pass (PROMPT.md).
- **XR-08 Tenancy, scope and personal data.** Runtime connections use `erev_app` behind the role guard (DG-ENV-12), with the tenant set by `SET LOCAL` per transaction (D-42). Handlers check entity scope with `require_for_entity`, and out-of-scope ids return 404 (DG-CMD-01; REQ-PLT-012). Export, posting and conversion commands call `ensure_production` once sandboxes exist (REQ-PLT-022). Logs carry no personal data (DG-LOG-03, DG-LOG-07), and secrets are read only through `SecretStore` (DG-ENV-17).
- **XR-09 Seed extension.**
  - From the first WEB seed item onward, an item that adds user-visible data, or a capability that a seeded tenant uses, extends the `erev seed demo` builders in `backend/erev_api/domain/demo/`. Screens then render PRD §2 content (REQ-DEMO-006).
  - Builders run domain commands as persona users, with maker and checker as different personas (WLD-R-02); direct inserts are allowed only for global catalogues. Output is deterministic with seed `20260912` (WLD-R-01; REQ-DEMO-007).
  - The seed refuses non-demo tenants and users outside `demo.erev` (WLD-R-04), takes passwords only from `EREV_DEMO_PASSWORD` (DG-RUN-32) and never touches `perf-volume` (DG-PERF-06).
- **XR-10 User interface.**
  - A screen item is complete when every region, binding, state, copy string and test hook of its screen ids exists and `screens.spec.ts` captures them (SCREENS SCR-IA-00).
  - States follow SCREENS SCR-ST-01 to SCR-ST-12 (DG-FE-14), permission gating SCR-PERM-01 to SCR-PERM-07, URL parameters SCREENS §0.5, and chips SCREENS §0.8 and SCREENS_B §0.4.
  - Only DS-CMP components and design tokens are used (DG-FE-09); `make design-check` and `make vocab-check` stay clean (D-62). Both themes, comfortable density, keyboard tables and WCAG 2.2 AA apply, with no serious or critical axe violation (DG-E2E-07).
  - Route objects carry `id` and `handle` per SCREENS SCR-IA-06 and DG-FE-02. Reads pass `as_of` for the context period (BR-UX-02); commands go through `useCommand` (DG-FE-05); dates go through the format module (DG-FE-20).
  - Captures are named per BS-D-09. After `make e2e` the loop reads both themes of each capture it added or changed, records a finding in `PROGRESS.md` before fixing it, and fixes deviations before ticking (PROMPT.md).
- **XR-11 AI.** AI follows DG-AI-01 to DG-AI-09. `FakeProvider` is the only provider under `test`, `e2e` and perf runs. Anthropic SDK code lives only in `backend/erev_api/adapters/ai/anthropic.py`, is written after reading the `claude-api` skill documentation, and is tested only against a mocked SDK client. AI output is a proposal; acceptance is an audited human command (D-46; CTL-045).
- **XR-12 Fail closed.**
  - When an item consumes a signal that a later item produces (unacknowledged journal batches before export exists, judgement review status before close gates, interface control totals before imports), the missing producer yields the conservative outcome: gate blocked, not certified, not auto-approved, not posted. A test proves it, and the producing item re-runs that test with the real signal.
  - Engine invariants raise `ENGINE_INVARIANT_VIOLATED` (DG-ENG-05; CTL-012), and decision commands roll back on engine errors (DG-CMD-09).
  - Unknown literals, unmapped roles or accounts, and missing FX rates return 04 §15.2 problems or §15.4 findings, never silent defaults.
- **XR-13 Registry completeness.** Registries checked by DG-ARC-08 grow through `PENDING_<REGISTRY>` tuples that later items empty (BS-D-07). An item that builds a handler removes its literal from the tuple in the same commit.
- **XR-14 No placeholder UI.** No placeholder pages, "coming soon" copy, TODO stubs or disabled features presented as built. The rail, the settings index, route tab bars and the command palette list only built routes (SCREENS SCR-IA-01 to SCR-IA-03). Landing routes follow BS-D-08.
- **XR-15 API surface.** Routes follow dev-guide §6.4 and 04 §15, declare their problem responses, and use DG-LST lists. `docs/api/openapi.json` and `frontend/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts` are regenerated by `make openapi` in the same commit (DG-LAY-07). Mock routes stay out of OpenAPI and out of `production` (D-72; DG-ARC-04).
- **XR-16 Documentation.** Operational or user-visible changes update the guides of BS-D-13, and security-relevant changes update `docs/security/` (DG-DONE-07). Under `docs/`, only `docs/api/`, `docs/guides/` and `docs/security/` are writable by the loop (DG-LAY-01).
- **XR-17 Shared machine and git.** The standing constraints of `docs/00-GOAL.md` §5 apply: ports, PID files, no `/tmp` (DG-RUN-30), only the three databases, no database or role administration (DG-FORBID-03), and no network except `make setup` (DG-MK-00f). Git follows DG-GIT-01 to DG-GIT-06 and DG-FORBID-05. No process the item started is left running (DG-DONE-09).
- **XR-18 Spec questions (D-77).** Gaps and conflicts go under **Spec questions** in `PROGRESS.md` as `SPEC-Q-<n>` with both references and the interpretation taken, and the loop continues. When a gap makes an item impossible, the loop keeps the item unticked and continues with the next item that does not depend on it. `BLOCKED:` is used only when every remaining item depends on the obstacle (PROMPT.md).
- **XR-19 Order.** No item depends on a later item, except fail-closed consumers under XR-12. Within a phase, schema and API items precede the screens that bind them, and engine stages precede their platform consumers (PHASES §3).
- **XR-20 Engine purity.** `erev_engine` imports only the standard library and performs no database, filesystem, network, clock, randomness or float access (D-10; DG-ENG-01 to DG-ENG-03; DG-ARC-02). Iteration is deterministic (DG-ENG-02). Errors are 04 §15.4 codes plus the DG-ENG-06 engine codes, and the engine never returns partial output. `ENGINE_VERSION` changes follow DG-ENG-10.

## 5. Item template and sizing

### 5.1 Template

```markdown
- [ ] **<ID> <Title>.**
  - **Prerequisites:** <item ids; GATE-<previous code> for the first item of a phase>
  - **Scope:**
    - Paths: <dev-guide §1.1 paths created or changed>
    - Schema: <04 ids created or changed: T-…, E-…, DB-…; or "none">
    - API: <API-R rows and routes; or "none">
    - Engine: <stage, ENGINE_SPEC section and rule ids S<nn>-R-…; or "none">
    - Screens: <screen ids with RT rows and paths; or "none">
  - **Acceptance:**
    - Tests: <one line per test: node id and the assertion it makes>
    - Answer keys: <`make answer-keys ID=…` with the count that must pass; or "none">
    - Golden: <`make parity K=…` with the case count; or "none">
    - Controls: <CTL-nnn and the node id of the test exercising its failure path; or "none">
    - Screens: <screen id (RT-nn `/path`), capture names, states captured; or "none">
    - Journeys: <J-nn.s steps, J-nn-AC-n and J-nn-ALT-n ids; or "none">
    - Properties: <PROP:Pn and module; or "none">
    - REQs completed: <REQ ids>; REQs contributed: <REQ ids>
  - **Read:** <exact sections and ids to grep, for example "04 T-CON-05; 04 §16.3; ENGINE_SPEC_B §10.2.3; POLICIES ALG-02; SCREENS §4.4">
  - **Gates:** <GK ids with the exact commands>
```

### 5.2 Field rules

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| IT-01 | Ids are stable and follow BS-D-01. Titles name the capability, not the activity. |
| IT-02 | **Scope** lists every path, table, enum value and route the item creates. An item creates nothing outside its scope list. |
| IT-03 | **Acceptance** names concrete tests with inputs and expected outputs, problem slug and status, or finding code. "Tests pass" is not an acceptance criterion. |
| IT-04 | Money in acceptance is an exact string taken from PRD §2.8, an answer key, a POLICIES CHK row or an ENGINE_SPEC worked example. |
| IT-05 | **Read** lists precise section numbers and ids, so that the loop greps instead of reading whole documents (PROMPT.md). |
| IT-06 | **Gates** lists the exact commands of §3.1 for the item's kinds. |
| IT-07 | Supervisor items appended during the build use this template and add "Supervisor item" after the title. |

### 5.3 Sizing

| Id | Rule |
|---|---|
| SZ-01 | One item fits one loop iteration of at most about 75 minutes of agent work, gates included; aim for 30 to 60 minutes. |
| SZ-02 | An item is split when it exceeds any of these limits: one migration revision or eight new tables; one API-R row group or twelve routes with schemas and tests; one ENGINE_SPEC subsection group (for example ENGINE_SPEC_B §9.2.3 to §9.2.5) with its rules, CHK tests and worked examples; two complex screen ids (SF-03 frame, SF-05, SF-07) or four list and detail screen ids; one journey part of ten steps (BS-D-15); forty answer keys newly required to pass; twenty-five REQ ids completed. |
| SZ-03 | Every item leaves the product working and tested. There are no scaffolding-only items and no untested code. |
| SZ-04 | Several small items may be done in one iteration; each is ticked with its own evidence and committed separately (DG-GIT-01). |
| SZ-05 | An item the loop cannot finish stays under **In flight** with the split point recorded; a partial item is never ticked. After two iterations without finishing, the loop records a spec question proposing a split, and the supervisor inserts `<id>a`, `<id>b`. |
| SZ-06 | Gate time counts toward the budget. Late in the plan, `make e2e` seeds every demo tenant (up to 15 minutes, NFR-08), so screen and journey items keep their implementation small. |
| SZ-07 | Phase budgets are the indicative counts of PHASES §1. |
| SZ-08 | A sizing flag of `research-harness/buildspec/check_buildspec.py` check 11 that is not split is listed with its reason in Appendix C "Coverage waivers" (BSF-D-06). A waiver accepts the size; SZ-05 still applies |

## 6. Checkpoint items `GATE-<code>`

Each phase ends with this item. It verifies and records evidence; a defect found here is fixed in the same item, with its own test.

```markdown
- [ ] **GATE-<code> Phase <code> checkpoint.**
  - **Prerequisites:** every item of phase <code>
  - **Scope:** verification and evidence; fixes only for defects this checkpoint finds
  - **Acceptance:**
    - Exit criteria: every exit criterion of PHASES §1 row <code> holds, each with the evidence named there
    - Membership: every REQ of PHASES §6 for <code>, control of §7, route row and placement of §10, journey of §11 and make target of §13 assigned to <code> is cited by a ticked item, and each REQ is listed under "REQs completed" by exactly one item
    - Gates: the PHASES §4 row GATE-<code> is green on a clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty) after the last commit
  - **Read:** PHASES §1, §4 and the membership rows for <code>
  - **Gates:** GK-11
```

The tick in `PROGRESS.md` is a checkpoint block:

```markdown
- [x] GATE-<code> Phase <code> checkpoint
  - Evidence: make ci OK (…); make test-pg OK (…); <every PHASES §4 gate of the row with its counts>
  - Membership: REQs <n> of <n>; controls <n> of <n>; route rows <n> of <n>; journeys <n> of <n>; make targets <n> of <n>
  - Spec questions opened in this phase: <SPEC-Q ids or "none">
  - Supervisor verification needed: <entries or "none">
  - Commit: <short sha>
```

Rules:

- **Collapsing evidence.** At the checkpoint, the loop collapses the phase's ticked items in `PROGRESS.md` to one line each (id and commit), which keeps the file under 20 KB (PROMPT.md).
- **No pause.** The checkpoint does not pause the loop (BS-D-14). The loop continues with the next phase, and the supervisor reviews asynchronously.
- **Regressions.** A regression in an earlier phase that the checkpoint finds is fixed before the checkpoint is ticked (DG-GATE-02).

Each set is written with `grep` and `sort` into `.run/tmp/`, then compared with `comm -3` | Both comparisons print nothing; 409 of 409 requirements completed |

## 01 FND Foundation: repository, toolchain, gates and kernel base

### 01.1 Phase preamble

**Entry criteria.** Roles `erev_owner` and `erev_app` and databases `erev`, `erev_test` and `erev_e2e` are provisioned by the supervisor (D-42; DG-ENV-15). `docs/BUILD_SPEC.md` is assembled.

**Exit criteria (PHASES §1 row FND).**

1. The tree and layout rules of dev-guide §1.1 to §1.3 hold: the `backend/` uv project; the `frontend/` toolchain (DG-FE-01, 09, 12, 13, 17, 19, 20; DG-RUN-20 to 24); `scripts/`; `Makefile`; `LICENSE`; `NOTICE`; `README.md`; `.env.example`.
2. Every FND target of PHASES §13 exists with DG-MK-00a to 00h semantics, and `make setup` is idempotent.
3. Kernel: dev-guide §5.1; §5.2 engines, session factories and role guard over global tables; §5.8 with `PROBLEMS` equal to 04 §15.2; §5.9 API money types; §5.10; §5.18 over global tables; §6.4 route helpers; §6.6 logging; API-R-53 `healthz`, `readyz` and `openapi.json`.
4. The revisions for 04 §18 step 0001 and the FND tables of PHASES §5.1 exist and pass DG-MIG-05.
5. `erev registry-seed` covers POLICIES §1 and T-PLT-31; `controls.yaml` equals 03 §4.1; StrEnum mirrors of 04 §3 exist; `CATALOGUE` equals T-PLT-11.
6. Self-tested `design_check`, `vocab_check`, `licence_check`, `secrets_check` and `openapi_check` pass; `make fixtures` has committed legacy fixtures and a manifest (DG-PAR-02).
7. DG-ARC-01 to 06, 09, 10, 12 and 13 exist and pass.
8. The frontend toolchain has `theme-init.js`, the tokens copy and the DS-VER-01 and DS-VER-02 Vitest suites; the router holds no screen until WEB.
9. The guides of BS-D-13 exist with sections for what is built.
10. `make ci` and `make test-pg` are green.

**Gate scope at the exit (PHASES §4 row GATE-FND).** `make ci`; `make test-pg`; `erev controls-report --tags-only` inside `make lint`; `make setup` run twice with no change; `make backend` readiness 200, then stopped; `make fixtures CHECK=1`. `make e2e`, `make answer-keys`, `make parity` and `make properties` are not yet run.

**Membership (PHASES §5.1, §6.1, §13).** Tables T-PLT-11 `permission`, T-PLT-31 `registry_parameter` and T-REF-08 `currency`, plus 04 §18 step 0001. Requirements REQ-PLT-028, REQ-PLT-031, REQ-PLT-032, REQ-CTL-001, REQ-SEC-003, REQ-SEC-009, REQ-SEC-010, REQ-OPS-005, REQ-OPS-007, REQ-OPS-010, REQ-UX-010 and REQ-UX-011. Controls: none. Route rows: none. Journeys: none. Make targets `setup`, `backend`, `frontend`, `migrate`, `db-reset`, `revision`, `fixtures`, `tokens`, `registry-seed`, `openapi`, `fmt`, `lint`, `design-check`, `vocab-check`, `licence-check`, `secrets-check`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `test-pg` and `controls-report` (22).

## 02 EKC Engine kernel and test harnesses

**Entry criteria.** GATE-FND ticked. FND provides the registry module `backend/erev_api/registry/policies.py` with `POLICY_PARAMETERS` (DG-KRN-REG-04), the StrEnum mirrors `backend/erev_api/enums.py`, the architecture tests DG-ARC-01 to 06, 09, 10, 12 and 13, and the committed legacy fixtures with their manifest (DG-PAR-02).

**Exit criteria (PHASES §1 row EKC).** (1) `erev_engine` public modules of DG-ENG-07 other than stage packages: `money`, `currencies`, `dates`, `progress`, `canonical`, `trace`, `formulas` and `reevaluate`, `enums`, `rules`, `errors`, `guards`, `bundle`, `stages/state`, the `stages/__init__` constants and `ENGINE_VERSION`. (2) DG-ARC-02 purity, and the CHK unit tests of COV-C-01. (3) Answer-key loader of dev-guide §9.5.8 loading all 234 files with zero errors; `coverage()` reporting zero gaps; `run_engine` bundle assembly; `assert_checkpoints`; `test_answer_keys.py`; the `make answer-keys` report. (4) Strategies, Hypothesis profiles, P2, P3, the helper part of P4 and `make properties`.

**Gate scope at exit (PHASES §4 row GATE-EKC).** `make ci`; `make test-pg`; the loader and coverage unit tests inside `make ci`; `make properties` unfiltered; `erev controls-report --tags-only` inside `make lint`. `make e2e`, `make answer-keys` and `make parity` are not yet gates.

**Membership.** REQ-REC-019 (PHASES §6.2). Make targets DG-MK-answer-keys and DG-MK-properties (§13). Properties P2, P3 and the helper part of P4 (§12). CHK unit tests of COV-C-01 (§8.3). No control, route row, placement or journey.

          - For a timeline item carrying `expect_problem`, `run_engine` computes one step bundle for the item's combination group. The bundle holds the items with `seq` ≤ that item's `seq`, excluding earlier `expect_problem` items.
          - The step passes when `compute` raises `EngineError` whose `code` equals `expect_problem.code`. Otherwise the run records a mismatch with subject `timeline seq <n>`, field `expect_problem`, expected that code, and actual `computed` or the other code.

        - Witnesses of item JOB-FAILED-ITEM-1 (header rev 1.158, fragment rev 1.18; supervisor ruling R-121 (n), from finding F-2 of lane ACCT's control inventory; the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-01 on the lane's pre-build line and on its correction of the item's severity; 03 rev 1.135, 04 rev 1.226, 05 rev 1.165, dev-guide rev 1.212, PRD rev 1.157; sub-bullets, so the item's criteria count is unchanged):
          - `::test_job_failed_item_1_who_learns_of_a_failed_job`: the same failure of a job started by the scheduler, by an API client and by a user — the log line `operator_alert.raised` of kind `JOB_FAILED` with its values-free fields for the first two and none for the third, the notification for the third alone, and `job.finish` for all three; `::test_job_failed_item_1_an_alert_that_cannot_be_raised_changes_nothing`.
          - `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_job_failed_items.py::test_job_failed_item_1_a_failed_job_of_an_entity_leaves_its_item`: a failed computation of a contract leaves one open `INFO` item `JOB_FAILED` of source `ENGINE` in the transaction that ends the job, naming the entity and the contract; a second failure counts it again; a preview and a job without a subject raise none; a later job of the kind and record that runs to its end resolves it as the system; a failure after that raises a new item.
          - `::test_job_failed_item_1_the_item_holds_no_close_and_is_dismissed_with_a_comment`: the count behind `blockers.exceptions_open` and the gate `EXCEPTIONS_CLEARED` leaves the open item out, where it counts a `WARNING` item of the same entity; `DISMISS` is among its actions and the command closes it with the comment.
          - `::test_job_failed_item_1_an_item_that_cannot_be_raised_leaves_the_job_failed` and `::test_job_failed_item_1_a_failure_hook_that_fails_leaves_nothing_behind`: a reader, a writer or a hook that raises is logged, leaves neither a row nor an audit event of a row that was rolled back, and the job ends `FAILED` with its `job.finish`.
          - `backend/tests/domain/imports/test_commit_job_failed.py::test_job_failed_item_1_a_stalled_commit_ends_its_upload_failed` and `backend/tests/domain/ssp/test_calculator_job_failed.py::test_job_failed_item_1_a_stalled_run_ends_failed`: an upload left `COMMITTING` and an SSP calculator run left `RUNNING` by a worker that died are ended `FAILED` by the kind's failure hook when the sweeper settles the job; a record that ended or that another transaction holds is left alone.
          - `backend/tests/pg/test_job_failed_readers.py::test_job_failed_item_1_the_readers_name_one_entity_or_none` (each reader on rows of its kind's subject) and `::test_job_failed_item_1_the_read_of_a_succeeding_job_is_one_probe_of_the_open_index`; `backend/tests/unit/test_job_failed_kinds.py::test_job_failed_item_1_the_kinds_that_leave_an_item_are_a_closed_list`.
        - Witnesses of item JOB-STALL-COMMIT-RACE-1 (header rev 1.233, fragment rev 1.34; found by lane OPS on 2026-10-02 with the commit of an import; the supervisor's ruling of 2026-10-02 on the lane's pre-build line; 05 rev 1.200, dev-guide rev 1.266, PRD rev 1.191; sub-bullets, so the item's criteria count is unchanged). The stalled notification of `test_ctl_040_stalled_job_failed_and_notified` reads "… no heartbeat for 10 minutes. The job was stopped; what it had not committed by then is not kept.":
          - `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_job_stall_rule.py::test_job_06_a_job_with_a_transaction_open_is_passed_over_and_ends_well` (three cases): a handler ten minutes and a second inside one transaction is passed over at every pass of the sweeper — `job.sweep_passed_over` with the job, its kind, the attempt and 601, then 661 seconds — its work commits and the job ends `SUCCEEDED` under the task that started it; on a last attempt, with attempts left (no second task is dispatched), and where the unit of work holds the job's row as well.
          - `::test_job_06_a_unit_of_work_of_a_stopped_job_is_refused_at_its_beginning`: silent outside a transaction, the job is stopped; the unit of work its handler opens next is refused before its work, the registry logs `job.attempt_lost` and records nothing, and the member reads the stopped job's body. `::test_job_06_a_commit_under_a_job_that_was_moved_keeps_nothing`: a job moved out of `RUNNING` beside an open unit of work — the commit finds no row for its heartbeat, and a handler that takes the refusal and leaves its block commits nothing by that.
          - `::test_job_04_a_beat_of_a_lost_attempt_is_refused_and_leaves_its_successors_row`: after the sweeper handed the job to a second attempt, the first attempt's heartbeat and progress raise and leave the second attempt's row as it is.
          - `::test_job_06_a_unit_that_begins_during_a_settlement_waits_and_is_refused`: a settlement held open in its failure hook; a unit of work of the attempt is read waiting for the job's lock in `pg_stat_activity`, blocked by the settlement's backend, and is refused once the settlement has committed.
          - `::test_dg_krn_db_08_a_jobs_unit_of_work_takes_its_locks_in_one_order`: read from the statements sent — the lock first, the read of the job's row second, the heartbeat directly before the audit chain's head. `::test_job_06_the_heartbeat_takes_no_key_of_the_job_row`: beside an open heartbeat a `FOR KEY SHARE NOWAIT` of the job's row is granted and a job under that parent is inserted and committed; the catalogue's list of the tables that refer to `job` is the eleven the dev guide names.
          - `::test_job_06_a_transaction_in_another_workspace_holds_the_lock_and_beats_first`: a unit of work in another workspace takes the lock and then writes the heartbeat in the job's workspace; the job is passed over while it is open, and once the job is stopped the next such unit and a session that enlists are refused before their work.
          - `::test_rb_07_an_operator_ends_the_transaction_of_a_job_that_is_passed_over`: the statement of runbook RB-07, taken from the runbook's text, names the backend of the job's open unit of work and no other; after `pg_terminate_backend` nothing of the transaction is kept and the job ends `FAILED` as after any error.
          - `::test_job_06_a_transport_job_rests_on_its_messages_claim`: the registered handler of `EMAIL_DELIVERY` through the worker, with a send that takes ten minutes outside a transaction — the job is handed to a second attempt, the message is recorded `DISPATCHED` once under its own claim, the first attempt stops at its beat and the second finds nothing due.
          - `backend/tests/domain/imports/test_commit_job_failed.py::test_job_06_a_commit_in_flight_keeps_its_job_from_being_stopped`: the measured case turned round — a unit of work that holds the upload's row keeps the commit job from being stopped, and ends the upload `COMMITTED` under the job that is still its own.
          - `backend/tests/unit/test_job_unit_doors.py::test_dg_krn_job_04_a_transaction_of_a_job_passes_the_door_or_is_listed` with `::test_dg_krn_job_04_the_scan_tells_a_door_from_a_bare_transaction`: every transaction that can write and that a function handed a job context or a job runtime opens beside its units of work calls `enlist` first or stands in the closed list; `::test_dg_krn_job_04_an_attempt_and_a_context_with_a_job_row_are_the_registrys`; `::test_dg_krn_db_08_the_jobs_lock_is_a_read_a_copy_step_may_send`; `::test_ntf_05_the_body_of_a_stopped_job_says_what_was_not_kept`.
          - `backend/tests/unit/test_uow.py::test_krn_uow_02_before_commit_steps_and_a_commit_that_fails`: the steps run before the commit in their order, and a commit that fails at a step or at the chain leaves no transaction open; `backend/tests/unit/docs/test_guides.py::test_runbook_tells_a_job_that_is_passed_over_and_what_ends_it`.
          - `backend/tests/pg/test_rls_index_plans.py::test_a_jobs_unit_of_work_reaches_its_job_through_the_primary_key`: the read of the job's row where a unit of work begins and the heartbeat at its commit are each one probe of the primary key, with half of the tenant's three hundred jobs live.
      - `::test_krn_job_05_last_attempt_problem_stored`: the final `job.problem` is an RFC 9457 object with `type` `https://erev.dev/problems/job-stalled`.
      - `backend/tests/api/test_jobs_api.py::test_api_s_job_shape_and_access`: `GET /jobs/{id}` returns `id`, `kind`, `state`, `progress {done, total}`, `result`, `problem`, `created_by`, `created_at`, `started_at` and `finished_at`; another user without `audit.read` receives 404 `not-found`; a holder of `audit.read` for all entities receives 200 (fragment rev 1.15; 04 API-C-03 rev 1.219); `GET /jobs?kind=RETENTION_SWEEP&state=SUCCEEDED` filters.
      - `::test_r_50_a_cancel_writes_job_cancel_as_the_caller` (header rev 1.37; supervisor rulings R-50 (a), R-62 (b)): a cancellation that changes the job writes `job.cancel` as the caller under the response's request id — for a `RUNNING` job the request, followed by `job.finish` with state `CANCELLED` when the handler stops; for a `QUEUED` job the terminal event itself; a repeated request, a refused one and a request for another member's job write nothing. `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_job_monitoring.py::test_r_50_a_a_job_that_cannot_be_settled_never_stops_the_sweep` (dev-guide DG-KRN-JOB-06 rev 1.89): the sweeper settles each job in isolation — the stalled job of a tenant whose audit chain cannot take `job.finish` stays as it is and the stalled job of the tenant after it ends `FAILED` with its event.
      - `::test_cancel_between_chunks`: `POST /jobs/{id}/cancel` sets `cancel_requested_at`; a chunked test handler observes `cancel_requested()` after its current chunk and the job ends `CANCELLED`.

no secret can be issued for it, and the audit trail names the request that closed it. `::test_r38_the_bootstrap_admin_in_setup_gets_the_client_and_its_secret_at_once`: the request of the bootstrap Tenant Admin alone in setup shows the rule, not a person, and the secret authenticates at once. `::test_apr_setup_rule_2_a_client_requested_when_setup_completion_is_due_waits_for_a_person`: once the conditions of PRD BR-PLT-02 hold the client waits for a person — also where no command has set the stamp — and the creating command sets it (04 T-PLT-01 rev 1.168); ## 04 WEB Frontend foundation, platform screens and e2e harness

### 04.1 Phase preamble

**Entry criteria.** GATE-PLF is ticked. No other entry criterion (PHASES §1 row WEB).

**Exit criteria (PHASES §1 row WEB).**

1. The frontend source layout of dev-guide §8.1; the format module and i18n (DS-VER-03; DESIGN_SYSTEM §9); DS-CMP-01 to DS-CMP-32 with DS-VER-04 tests; the design gallery X:design (DS-VER-06).
2. The shell of SCREENS §1 with a rail listing built destinations only, and the WEB screens and placements of PHASES §10.
3. The Playwright harness DG-E2E-01 to DG-E2E-12: five projects, `personas` with TOTP, `screens.capture`, `a11y.check`, the network guard and `tenants.ts`; `scripts/e2e.sh` (BS-D-20); `screens.spec.ts` rows for the WEB screens; `design.spec.ts` (DS-VER-06 to DS-VER-09).
4. The `erev seed demo` scaffold: tenants WLD-T-00 to WLD-T-07 with code, display name, kind, `is_demo` and reporting currency (PRD §2.4); persona users WLD-U-01 to WLD-U-11 with memberships and roles (§2.3); TOTP factors (WLD-U-R2); `.run/demo-credentials.txt` (DG-RUN-32); `make seed` and `make e2e`.

**Gate scope at the exit (PHASES §4 row GATE-WEB).** `make ci`; `make test-pg`; `make e2e` unfiltered with BS-D-20 skips; the answer-key loader and coverage unit tests inside `make ci`; `make properties` unfiltered; `erev controls-report --tags-only` inside `make lint`; the light and dark screenshots of every WEB capture read and compared with SCREENS, SCREENS_B and DESIGN_SYSTEM.

**Membership (PHASES §6.4, §10, §13, §15.2).** Requirements REQ-PLT-004, 005, 006, 008, 009, 010, 013, 017, 021, 033, 036, REQ-CTL-006, REQ-SEC-004, REQ-SEC-008, REQ-OPS-016, REQ-UX-001, 002, 006, 007, 008, 009, 012, 013, 016, 021 and 022 (26). Route rows RT-01 to RT-06, RT-54 to RT-58, RT-71 to RT-73, RT-87 to RT-93, RT-97, RT-98, RT-108, RT-109, RT-111 and RT-112 (27). Placements SF-21, SF-23, SF-27, X:session-expiring, X:route-error and X:narrow-viewport. Make targets `seed` and `e2e`. `E2E` hints closing in WEB (§15.2): REQ-PLT-021, REQ-SEC-008, REQ-UX-007, REQ-UX-013, REQ-UX-022. Controls: none. Journeys: none.

**Captures (BS-D-09).** Capture names are the SCR-TID-03 normalisation of the screen id plus an optional state slug. Every screen item appends its rows to `frontend/e2e/projects/screens.spec.ts`, runs `a11y.check` on each surface, and requires the loop to read `frontend/e2e/.screens/screens/<nn>-<capture>.light.png` and `.dark.png` for each capture, compare them with the SCREENS, SCREENS_B and DESIGN_SYSTEM sections cited, and record any finding in `PROGRESS.md` before fixing it (XR-10; GK-07).

        - a wrong TOTP code or recovery code writes `MFA_CHALLENGE_FAILED`;
        - the fifth such event for the user after the later of `user_mfa_factor.updated_at` and `app_user.locked_until` sets `locked_until` to now + 15 minutes, writes `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` and answers 423 `account-locked`;
        - while `locked_until` is in the future, the route answers 423 `account-locked` without verifying.
      - `backend/erev_api/domain/platform/users.py` (D-80 MFA reset):
        - `reset_mfa` refuses a membership that is neither `ACTIVE` nor `SUSPENDED` with 409 `invalid-transition` (`errors[0].field == "status"`) before any write. A target whose `app_user.is_operator` is true answers 404 `not-found`;
        - `reset_mfa` writes `user_mfa_factor.reset` in the tenant of every ACTIVE membership of the user, as `auth/mfa.py` `_audit_enrolment` does (04 T-PLT-04; SPEC-Q-182 (d) overruled);
        - `invite_user` refuses an email whose `app_user.is_operator` is true with 422 `validation-failed` on `email`, rule `T-PLT-02`, message "This email cannot be invited to a workspace."
      - `backend/erev_api/approvals/subjects.py`:
        - `_apply_role_assignment` locks the membership row `FOR UPDATE` before `sod.assert_assignment_allowed`;
        - `_apply_role_change` locks the membership of every holder of the role, in ascending id order, before `sod.assert_role_change_allowed` (DG-CMD-02; precedent `users._lock_membership`).
      - `backend/erev_api/audit/verify.py` (D-80 chain anchoring):
        - `verify_tenant_chain` compares the last checked event with `audit_chain_head`, read in the same transaction;
        - `record_tenant_verification` compares the latest earlier PASS row's `to_chain_seq` event with its `digest_last_hmac`.
      - `backend/erev_api/db/migrations/versions/0025_audit_chain_head_guard.py`, created with `make revision MSG="audit chain head guard" ITEM=WEB-3a`:

        - the trigger refuses with `EREV-AUD-001` any update issued outside `tg_audit_event__chain` (`pg_trigger_depth() < 2`) or not setting `last_chain_seq = OLD.last_chain_seq + 1`;

        - Setup: user U with a confirmed factor signs in with the password only (`mfa_verified_at` null) in an earlier FrozenClock minute.
        - Within one minute from one client address, wrong codes to `POST /api/v1/session/mfa` give:
          - attempts 1 to 4: 422 `validation-failed`;
          - attempt 5: 423 `account-locked`;
          - attempts 6 to 10: 423 without verification;
          - attempt 11: 429 `rate-limited` with a `Retry-After` header.
        - `MFA_CHALLENGE_FAILED` is written 5 times and `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` once.
        - Ten other users, signed in during an earlier minute, each send 5 wrong codes from one address within one minute (50 requests). The 51st request from that address, for an eleventh user, returns 429 `rate-limited` and writes no `MFA_CHALLENGE_FAILED`.

        - The review probe `test_probe_mfa_challenge_unthrottled` observed 150 × 422 in this situation.
      - `backend/tests/api/test_mfa.py::test_ctl_033_mfa_lockout_after_five_failures` (PR-A-01):
        - U sends 4 wrong codes (422), signs in with the password again, then sends 1 wrong code: 423 `account-locked`. `app_user.locked_until` equals the FrozenClock time + 15 minutes.
        - While U is locked, a correct code returns 423, and the session's `mfa_verified_at` stays null.
        - For a second user, 4 wrong TOTP codes and 1 wrong recovery code lock the account.
        - 15 minutes later U's correct code returns 200, and a following wrong code returns 422.
        - `test_ctl_033_mfa_required_permission_blocks_until_verified`, `test_recovery_code_single_use` and `test_bs1_d_19_step_up_window` still pass.

        - Setup: setup completed. Member M holds no role and has two `PENDING` `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT` requests, for `revenue_accountant` and `revenue_reviewer`.
        - Approver A's `decide` of the first runs on its own connection and holds its transaction open after `_apply_role_assignment`.
        - Approver B's `decide` of the second runs on a second connection under `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '500ms'`. It raises lock-not-available (SQLSTATE `55P03`) and commits nothing.
        - After A commits, B's `decide` in a new transaction raises 409 `sod-conflict` naming `SoD-3` and rolls back. Then:

- [ ] **WEB-3c PLF review remediation, part 3: single-claim outbox and webhook dispatch, handler heartbeats and stranded-task recovery (PR-R-01, PR-R-02, PR-R-03, PR-R-04). Supervisor item.**
  - **Prerequisites:** GATE-PLF; WEB-3b
  - **Scope:**
    - Paths:
      - `backend/erev_api/events/webhooks.py` `_claim`, `_attempt`, `_record` and `deliver` (D-80 dispatch and job recovery; SPEC-Q-189 (c) corrected):
        - one due delivery is claimed (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, with `next_attempt_at` = now + 120 s as the claim stamp) and committed, then posted, then recorded only where `next_attempt_at` still equals the stamp;
        - zero recorded rows means another deliverer settled the delivery, and the run continues without raising;
        - `jc.heartbeat()` runs after each delivery, with at most 100 deliveries per run.
      - `backend/erev_api/events/outbox.py` `_claim`, `_dispatch`, `_relay` and `relay`:
        - the same single-claim loop over messages, with `updated_at` as the claim stamp;
        - the ADP-32 re-claim takes only messages whose own stamp is older than 15 minutes;
        - `jc.heartbeat()` runs after each message.
      - `backend/erev_api/domain/platform/audit_jobs.py`: `jc.heartbeat()` at least every 1,000 verified events or 30 seconds.
      - `backend/erev_api/jobs/registry.py` `run_job` and `_move`:
        - completion is recorded only on the RUNNING row of the attempt that ran (same `procrastinate_job_id` and attempt number);
        - `_defer_unless_pending` counts only QUEUED rows whose Procrastinate task is `todo` or `doing`.
      - `backend/erev_api/jobs/sweeper.py` (05 JOB-06 part one and SCH-04; SPEC-Q-187 (b) overruled):
        - re-dispatches QUEUED job rows whose Procrastinate task is `failed`, `cancelled` or `aborted`, within the kind's retry profile;
        - retries tasks stalled in `doing` found through `JobManager.get_stalled_jobs` (worker heartbeats), using `retry_job_by_id` (Procrastinate 3.9.0);
        - past the last attempt, the row ends `FAILED` with problem `job-stalled`.
      - `backend/erev_api/worker.py`: only if the periodic sweeper wiring changes.
      - Tests: `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_webhooks.py`, `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_outbox.py`, `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_job_monitoring.py`, `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_jobs.py`.
      - The runbook sections "Stuck and failed jobs" and "Outbound webhooks" (SPEC-Q-187 a; SPEC-Q-189 a).
    - Schema: none
    - API: none
    - Engine: none
    - Screens: none

        - Setup: three `period.locked` events are emitted to one active endpoint.
        - An SCH-12 `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY` job posts the first delivery. The recording transport then advances the FrozenClock 121 s and runs a second `deliver()` to completion before the first job continues.
        - Every envelope id is posted exactly once, every delivery is `DELIVERED` after one attempt, and both jobs end `SUCCEEDED`.
        - The review probe A observed `[1, 2, 2]` POSTs and two `invalid-transition` failures.
        - `test_retry_backoff_and_abandon` and `test_inactive_endpoint_abandons_delivery` still pass.
      - `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_outbox.py::test_adp_32_live_relay_not_reclaimed` (PR-R-02):
        - Setup: three `EMAIL` messages are enqueued.
        - Relay 1 dispatches the first message. The fake email adapter then advances the clock 15 minutes and runs relay 2 to completion before relay 1 continues.
        - The fake email directory holds exactly three files, every message is `DISPATCHED`, and both relays end `SUCCEEDED`.
        - A message left `DISPATCHING` by a relay that stopped is still re-claimed and sent once after 15 minutes.
        - The review probe B observed `[1, 2, 2]` sends.
        - `test_krn_evt_05_relay_backoff_and_dead_letter` still passes.
      - `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_job_monitoring.py::test_krn_job_04_heartbeat_keeps_long_handlers_running` (PR-R-03):
        - A `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY` run over 70 due deliveries uses a recording transport that advances the FrozenClock 10 s per POST and calls `sweeper.fail_stalled(runtime)` after every sixth POST. The run stays `RUNNING` throughout, ends `SUCCEEDED`, posts 70 times and is never re-queued.
        - A user's `OUTBOX_RELAY` over 70 messages with the same clock pattern ends `SUCCEEDED`, and no `JOB_FAILED` notification is written.
        - `test_ctl_040_stalled_job_failed_and_notified` still passes.
      - `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_job_monitoring.py::test_run_job_records_only_its_own_attempt` (PR-R-03):
        - Setup: attempt 1 of a `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY` job is `RUNNING`. After 10 minutes 1 second without a heartbeat, the sweeper re-queues it, and attempt 2 moves the row to `RUNNING`.
        - When attempt 1's handler returns, the row stays `RUNNING` under attempt 2 and no result is stored.
        - Attempt 2's completion sets `SUCCEEDED`.
        - The review probe V5 observed attempt 1 marking attempt 2's row `SUCCEEDED`.
      - `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_jobs.py::test_krn_job_06_stranded_tasks_redispatched` (PR-R-04):
        - Setup: an `OUTBOX_RELAY` job is dispatched, and `registry.job_concurrency` is patched to raise `OperationalError`. `run_job` raises, and the Procrastinate task ends `failed` while the row stays `QUEUED`.
        - `outbox.sweep` still defers a relay for the tenant while due messages exist.
        - `sweeper.sweep` re-dispatches the job with a new `procrastinate_job_id`, and the job then ends `SUCCEEDED`.
        - A `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY` task stalled in `doing`, whose worker stopped sending heartbeats (`get_stalled_jobs` with `seconds_since_heartbeat` 30), is retried the same way.
        - `defer_for_active_tenants` again defers `AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY` and `RETENTION_SWEEP` for the tenant.
        - Review probes C and V6 observed the job still `QUEUED` and 0 deferrals two days later.
        - `test_krn_job_06_sweeper_requeues_undispatched_jobs` still passes.

## 06 RFD Reference data, policies and SSP studio

Author BS-3. Uses PLF, WEB and ENA (PHASES §1 row 6). Indicative size 20 items; this phase holds 25 items and GATE-RFD.

- **Entry criteria.** GATE-ENA ticked. No other entry criterion.
- **Exit criteria (PHASES §1 row 6).** (1) API-R rows of PHASES §5.2 for RFD with schemas 04 §16.4, §16.5 and the period reads of §16.8; commands routed through the RFD subjects of §5.3. (2) RFD tables of §5.1 and the provisioning extensions of §5.3. (3) SSP publication with range validation `erev_api.domain.ssp.range_validation.validate_ranges` (DG-AK-45; CHK-031); SSP resolution through `s05_allocation.resolve_ssp`; SSP calculator job; legacy-parity preset command (DG-KRN-REG-05). (4) RFD screens of §10 with captures, including SF-15:setup and the context pill binding (BS-D-17). (5) Tagged tests of §7 for RFD.
- **Gate scope at exit (PHASES §4 row GATE-RFD).** `make ci`; `make test-pg`; `make e2e` unfiltered; answer keys: loader and coverage unit tests inside `make ci`; `make parity`: not yet; `make properties` unfiltered; `make controls-report`: `--tags-only` inside `make lint`; no perf; no extra evidence.
- **Membership (PHASES §5.1 to §5.3, §6.6, §7, §10, §15.2).** Tables (29): T-REF-01 to T-REF-07, T-REF-09 to T-REF-23, T-REF-28 to T-REF-34. API: API-R-13 (registry routes; the policy-override routes are CTR-15, BS3-D-04), API-R-17, API-R-18 (calendars, `generate-year`, period reads, `open`), API-R-19 to API-R-27, API-R-57. Subjects `SSP_BOOK_VERSION`, `REGISTRY_VERSION`, `RULE_SET_VERSION`, `POB_TEMPLATE_VERSION`, `ACCOUNT_MAPPING_VERSION`, `FX_RATE_SET_VERSION`, `PRINCIPAL_AGENT_CHANGE`. Job kind `SSP_CALCULATOR` (and `POLICY_SIMULATION`, BS3-D-17). Provisioning rows: `book` rows `ASC606`, `IFRS15`, `LEGACY`; built-in `dimension_definition` rows; `tenant_currency` for the reporting currency; JE numbering series when an entity is created. Requirements: the 32 of PHASES §6.6. Controls: CTL-010, CTL-011, CTL-031. Route rows (23): RT-59 to RT-70, RT-74 to RT-83, RT-110. `E2E` hint closed here: REQ-UX-002.

- A failing key is fixed in the engine or runner code, never in the key (DG-PAR-09 analogue; PROMPT.md "never edit expected values"). The fix commit message cites the ENGINE_SPEC or POLICIES rule it implements.

- Each item re-runs the selections of the earlier AKS items (and END-9) before ticking, so a regression is fixed inside the item (DG-GATE-02).

## 13 GPA Golden parity: contract and probe kinds

**Entry criteria.** GATE-DIN ticked (PHASES §3 order AKS → CTR → DIN → GPA). GPA consumes these interfaces:
- the DIN legacy v1 import pipeline, 04 API-R-43 (`POST /imports`, validate, diff, submit, approve, commit), with the four legacy templates of 04 §17.4;
- the RFD preset command `create_preset_version` (DG-KRN-REG-05) through the registry version lifecycle;
- the CTR contract, obligation-version and calculation-trace stores and queries (API-R-28 to API-R-36, API-R-49);
- the committed fixtures of DG-PAR-02 (GATE-FND).

**Exit criteria (PHASES §1 row GPA, as adjusted by B3-BS2-04).** The parity runner of DG-PAR-01 to 11 runs over the legacy v1 pipeline under the `LEGACY_PARITY` preset. `make parity K="initial_allocation or pob_position or contract_position or cumulative_catchup or probe-P3-over-delivery-validation"` passes 94 of 94, and the DG-PAR-08 report is written. Probes P1, P2 and P4 close in GPB-1.

**Gate scope at exit (PHASES §4 row GATE-GPA, B3-BS2-04).** `make ci`; `make test-pg`; `make e2e` unfiltered; `make answer-keys ID=<§8.2.1 ids>` (221 keys); `make parity K="initial_allocation or pob_position or contract_position or cumulative_catchup or probe-P3-over-delivery-validation"` (94 cases); `make properties` unfiltered; `erev controls-report --tags-only` inside `make lint`; the parity report counts by kind as extra evidence.

**Membership.** No requirement is completed (PHASES §6.13); GPA closes `GT:` and `GT-nn` hints of §9 kinds `initial_allocation`, `pob_position`, `contract_position`, `cumulative_catchup` and probe P3 of `legacy_probe`. Make target DG-MK-parity (§13).

## 14 EDS Engine stage 15: close projections and disclosures

**Entry criteria.** GATE-GPA ticked. `compute` runs stages 02 to 14 (END-9), and `PENDING_STAGES == (("15", "EDS"),)`.

**Exit criteria (PHASES §1 row EDS).** The stage 15 engine part of ENGINE_SPEC_B §15.2 exists, with invariants, findings and worked examples: RPO and time bands, rollforwards, prior-period revenue, disaggregation, cost rollforward, lock snapshot content and variance between closes. The keys of PHASES §8.2.2 pass, and P7 holds for the engine part. The platform report runs, snapshot storage and variance jobs are CLO and RPS (B3-BS2-10).

**Gate scope at exit (PHASES §4 row GATE-EDS).** `make ci`; `make test-pg`; `make e2e` unfiltered; `make answer-keys ID=<§8.2.1 and §8.2.2 ids>` (227 keys); `make parity` with the GATE-GPA selection (94 cases, B3-BS2-04); `make properties` unfiltered; `erev controls-report --tags-only` inside `make lint`.

**Membership.** 2 requirements (PHASES §6.14): REQ-CST-006, REQ-FX-007. PROP:P7 engine part (§12). Keys of §8.2.2 (6 `DISC` engine-runner keys). No control, route row, placement, journey or make target.

**Entry criteria.** GATE-FCS ticked (PHASES §1 row 22).

**Exit criteria (PHASES §1 row AIX).** T-AI-01 and T-AI-02; API-R-47 and `POST /tenant/ai/disable`; provider interface DG-AI-01 to DG-AI-09 with `FakeProvider` and the Anthropic adapter tested only against a mocked SDK client; `AI_TASK`; contract review proposals and acceptance; explain narratives with number validation; anomaly flags; revenue Q&A with citations; budget and kill switch; SF-20 screens, SF-28, SF-15:ai and SF-15:ai-call-log; DG-ARC-11; CTL-045.

- REQs (10): REQ-AI-001, REQ-AI-002, REQ-AI-003, REQ-AI-004, REQ-AI-005, REQ-AI-006, REQ-AI-007, REQ-AI-008, REQ-AI-009, REQ-AI-010.

  - **Prerequisites:** SOP-6
  - **Scope:**
    - Paths: `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_audit_coverage.py`; `backend/tests/support/audit_catalogue.py` (the REQ-PLT-019 categories mapped to the audit actions the product writes); fixes in any command handler that lacks its audit event
    - Schema: none
    - API: none
    - Engine: none
    - Screens: none
  - **Acceptance:**
    - Tests:
      - `backend/tests/domain/platform/test_audit_coverage.py::test_ctl_038_every_command_route_writes_audit`: for every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE operation of the committed `docs/api/openapi.json` other than (a) `POST /session/login`, `POST /session/mfa`, the password-reset routes, `POST /oauth/token` and `POST /operator/tenants`, (b) stateless evaluations that return a result and persist nothing (the evaluate and explain-verify operations; a preview that defers a job is not one, see below) and (c) the 04 §1.7 AUD-OPS personal read markers, preferences and saved views (`me_notifications_read`, `me_notifications_read_all`, `me_notification_preferences_put`, `me_preferences_update`; `saved_views_create`, `saved_views_update`, `saved_views_delete`, rev 1.25), a successful call in a fresh tenant writes at least one `audit_event` in the same transaction, with `action` matching `^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+$`, `request_id` equal to the response `X-Request-Id`, and `actor_kind` of the caller; the routes of (a) write `security_event` rows instead (login, failed login, MFA, password reset) or the provisioning events of DG-KRN-TEN-01. The exemptions of (b) and (c) are defined by class here and enumerated as the `query` class of `backend/tests/support/audit_catalogue.py`, each named in the test's failure message and in the lane record; the walk additionally asserts that a `query` operation persists nothing except the 04 §1.7 personal rows (zero `audit_event` rows and zero other writes), so the label can never hide a mutation. The persistence boundary the walk measures is explicit: the `idempotency_record` row that `run_command` writes for every command (04 §1.7 AUD-OPS; `idempotency/store.py`) is infrastructure allowed on every path, `query` operations included, and nothing else is — a queued `job` row is not routine infrastructure. A command that starts a job is a job-starting command in the audited class, not a stateless evaluation: `POST /contracts/{id}/events/preview` and `POST /estimate-versions/{id}/preview` defer a `CONTRACT_COMPUTE` dry run (`uow.defer` inserts the `job` row in the command's transaction and dispatches after commit) and return 202, so they leave class (b); 04 T-PLT-27 AUD-OPS audits the commands that start and finish jobs, and their audit evidence is the job-start `audit_event` written in the same transaction as the `job` row (the jobs registry writes it on every deferral of a unit of work: `job.start`, as the caller and under the command's request id — 04 T-PLT-27 rev 1.106, supervisor rulings R-50 (a) and R-62 (a), header rev 1.37; until then no deferral left an audit event and the three previews, `POST /jobs/{id}/cancel` and `POST /audit-events/verify` failed this walk). The exemption is not widened for queued work, and the catalogue's exact-set unit test is a declaration, not proof: only the walk proves that a `query` operation writes nothing (D-98 candidate 49, supervisor ruling of 2026-09-20). `POST /session/invitations/lookup` is not exempt: a lookup with an unknown, expired or malformed token is a probing signal and writes a `security_event` (an invitation-token failure kind of the E-79 vocabulary); a successful lookup writes none (D-98 (20), supervisor ruling of 2026-09-19). Class (d), idempotent confirms (SOP7-PUBLISH-CONFIRM-1; rev 1.16): `POST /account-mappings/{id}/publish`, `POST /pob-template-versions/{id}/publish`, `POST /rule-set-versions/{id}/publish`, `POST /policies/{id}/publish` and `POST /import-mapping-profiles/{id}/publish` stay REQUIRED but their state change is performed and audited by the approval that precedes them (04 §16.5: the final approval publishes in the approval transaction; `lifecycle.approve` and `mapping.approve` call `publish`, which returns a PUBLISHED version as it is), so for them "at least one `audit_event` in the same transaction, with `request_id` equal to the response `X-Request-Id`, and `actor_kind` of the caller" is read on the APPROVAL transaction: the `<table>.published` row under the FINAL approving request's `X-Request-Id` and `actor_kind`, never on the confirm's own request, which writes no transition audit and only the `idempotency_record` infrastructure row. The walk credits a class-(d) operation only when it correlates, in one tenant, the table, the version-row UUID, the business approval id, the final approving request id, the SUCCESS `APPROVED → PUBLISHED` event and its actor, then issues a DISTINCT fresh confirmation (a fresh `Idempotency-Key`, not an idempotent replay) that returns the same PUBLISHED version, and compares the bounded subject state (status, `row_version`, `updated_at`, content hash) before and after the confirmation as unchanged; zero audit rows alone proves neither the absence of an update nor the handler's execution. The class is enumerated as the `confirm` class of `backend/tests/support/audit_catalogue.py` with its publication literal noted as f-string-built (`lifecycle.transition`: `f"{kind.object_type}.{status}"`) and verified at runtime, not statically. The `APPROVED`-left-unpublished `publish` branch (a version whose approval did not publish it) is a separate path the class does not cover. For the signature-verified webhook receiver (`webhooks_receive`, ADP-01; rev 1.19) the recorded actor is the tenant's system principal, `actor_kind` SYSTEM: the unauthenticated receiver's caller is the adapter and the product records it under `system_principal` by design, so the walk's caller-kind check admits SYSTEM for that one operation and names it in its failure message. Saved views (rev 1.25; supervisor ruling R-14 of 2026-09-29): class (c) is defined by the 04 §1.7 AUD-OPS class, and 04 T-PLT-37 classes `saved_view` — a user's saved grid filters, columns and favourites — AUD-OPS, so `POST /saved-views`, `PATCH /saved-views/{id}` and `DELETE /saved-views/{id}` belong to it; its first enumeration omitted them. The walk's persistence assertion holds for them as for every class (c) operation: zero `audit_event` rows, and nothing written but the caller's own `saved_view` row — the operation's 04 §1.7 personal row — and the `idempotency_record` infrastructure row. Class (e), a command the release refuses by name, which stores nothing (rev 1.44; item POLICY-OVERRIDE-WITHDRAW-1, register index 308; supervisor ruling R-126 (b) (4) and (c) and the supervisor's rulings of 2026-10-03 on the lane's line; 04 T-CON-23 "Not offered in release 1.0" rev 1.322; PRD ERR-102): `POST /policy-overrides` stays a command operation of the OpenAPI document and refuses every creation, so no successful call of it exists to evidence. It stays REQUIRED and is walked for its refusal: the call of a person who holds the permission, on a contract she reads, must answer 422 `policy-level-not-allowed` with rule id `POLICY_OVERRIDE_NOT_OFFERED`, write zero `audit_event` rows under its request id and change the row count of no tenant table, the `idempotency_record` infrastructure row apart, as for class (b); any other answer — a success above all — an audit row or a changed table fails the walk by name. The class is enumerated as the `refused` class of `backend/tests/support/audit_catalogue.py` (`RELEASE_REFUSED`), each operation with the rule id it must answer; the catalogue's unit test pins the class to exactly this one operation, and the walk, not the pin, proves that nothing is stored. The action `policy_override.create` leaves the catalogue with the code that wrote it: the REQ-PLT-019 category of configuration, policy, mapping and SSP changes keeps its other five actions. `POST /policy-overrides/{id}/submit` stays in the audited class; the walk's world writes the DRAFT row it submits (`support.rows.insert_policy_override`), since the product creates none.
      - `::test_req_plt_019_categories_covered`: the audit actions observed while running one end-to-end fixture scenario include, per REQ-PLT-019 category: login and logout (`security_event` `LOGIN_SUCCEEDED`, `LOGIN_FAILED`, `LOGOUT`), MFA changes (`MFA_ENROLLED`, `MFA_RESET`), role, permission and SoD changes (`role.create`, `role_assignment.create`, `sod_exception.create`), configuration, policy, mapping and SSP changes (`registry_version.publish`, `ssp_book_version.approve`, `account_mapping_version.publish`), imports (`import_upload.upload`, `import_upload.validate`, `import_upload.approve`, `import_upload.commit`), events submitted and voided (`contract_event.append`, `contract_event.void`), approvals and rejections (`approval_request.approve`, `approval_request.reject`), calculation and close runs (`contract_computation.persist`, `close_run.start`), period status changes (`period_state.closed`), journal lifecycle (`journal_run.approve`, `journal_batch.export`), report runs and exports (`report_run.create`), API client lifecycle (`api_client.create`, `api_client.revoke`), support grants (`support_grant.approve`) and AI proposal lifecycle (`ai_proposal.accept`). Each name is taken from the handler that implements it; a missing category fails the test with the category name.
      - `::test_denied_commands_audited`: for five command routes called by a principal lacking the permission, one `DENIED` audit event exists per call.

##### Decisions taken in B3 (D-77)

None of these opens a question. Each row is the most reasonable default within the BUILD_SPEC author's remit, and the items below apply it. Rows marked "interface" name another author's phase; the orchestrator relays them.

| BS1-D-01 | FND builds `backend/erev_engine/canonical.py` (dev-guide §5.17 complete) and `backend/erev_engine/currencies.py` (`CurrencySpec`, `ISO_4217`). EKC consumes both unchanged. The private exact formatter inside `canonical.py` equals the DG-KRN-MONEY `format_exact` contract (ROUND_HALF_UP at 18 places, trailing zeros trimmed, no exponent); EKC may replace it by a call to `erev_engine.money.format_exact` in a patch that changes no output. Interface: EKC (BS-2) | FND consumes both before EKC runs: `KeyRing.encrypt` uses the canonical bytes of its context as associated data (DG-KRN-KEY-04), and the `currency` seed comes from `ISO_4217` (DG-MIG-07; PHASES §5.1 FND table T-REF-08) |

| BS1-D-28 | System-written files without a dedicated E-68 purpose (idempotent responses above 1 MiB of DG-KRN-IDEM-04; access review snapshots of T-PLT-40) use purpose `REPORT_OUTPUT` | E-68 has no generic output purpose, and adding a value would change 04 |
| BS1-D-29 | SoD rule versions (`POST /sod-rules/{code}/versions`) move DRAFT → TESTED → SUBMITTED → APPROVED → PUBLISHED and route through subject `ROLE_CHANGE` with step permission `access.approve` | PRD SM-04 lists SoD rules under the configuration lifecycle, E-08 has no SoD rule subject, and access administrators approve role governance (PRD §2.5 routing row `ROLE_CHANGE`) |
| BS1-D-30 | `POST /session/login` returns 200 with the API-S-Session fields plus `csrf_token`, `mfa_required` and `mfa_enrolment_required`. A wrong email or password returns 401 `unauthenticated` with detail `The email or password is incorrect.`. A wrong TOTP or recovery code returns 422 `validation-failed` with `errors[0].field` `code` or `recovery_code` | SCREENS_B §12.1 names the next-step members; 04 §15.2 has no dedicated slug |
| BS1-D-31 | `POST /roles` inserts the custom role with `is_active = false` and no `role_permission` rows, and submits a `ROLE_CHANGE` request. Approval inserts the permissions and sets `is_active = true`. `POST /roles/{id}/propose-change` on a role with `is_system = true` returns 409 `invalid-transition` with detail `System roles cannot change.` | T-PLT-09 has no status column, and REQ-PLT-009 requires approval before a role takes effect |
| BS1-D-32 | `GET /me` `engine_release` is the T-PLT-38 row that the running process inserted at start, so PLF-20 (release stamping) precedes PLF-21 (`GET /me`) | 04 API-S-Me; 05 REL-03 |
| BS1-D-33 | The component items WEB-3 to WEB-7 precede the Playwright harness (WEB-11). They gate on their Vitest DS-VER-04 suites. WEB-24 builds the design gallery over every DS-CMP component and runs `make e2e SPEC=frontend/e2e/projects/design.spec.ts` for all of them (GK-07 for components) | The harness needs sign-in screens, which need the components; XR-19 forbids the reverse dependency |
| BS1-D-34 | The WEB top bar renders no context pill. WEB-9 builds DS-CMP-03 as a component and shows it in the design gallery; the RFD item that binds entities, periods and books adds it to the top bar | BS-D-17; a pill without entities would be a placeholder (XR-14) |
| BS1-D-35 | REQ-PLT-008 ("Role matrix export"), REQ-PLT-010 ("SoD conflict report as of any date") and REQ-PLT-033 ("API client inventory report") complete in WEB as PHASES §6.4 assigns. Their report surfaces RPT-24, RPT-25 and RPT-27 are built by RPS (BS1-D-14); the WEB items prove the data behind them through `conflict_report` and the list routes. Interface: RPS (BS-4) | BS-D-19 gives each REQ one build phase; the reports belong to the RPS framework (PHASES §5.4) |
| BS1-D-36 | `GET /metrics` is served by the api process only. Worker-side figures (job durations, queue depth, outbox messages) are read by the api from the database when the endpoint is scraped | 04 API-R-53 names api and worker processes, but a worker binds no port (DG-RUN-02) and no process may bind a port outside `docs/00-GOAL.md` §5 |
